title: A teacher who withholds advanced practices until students have the foundational capacities to use them protects the integrity of the work, not the teacher's status
body:
- Restriction of an advanced practice gates access on the recipient's readiness rather than on the rarity of the knowledge or the authority of the gatekeeper.
- Without foundational capacities — stable ethics, concentration, compassion, and the ability to distinguish formal technique from embodied knowing — the same practice becomes inert ritual or actively destabilising for the practitioner who attempts it.
- The arrangement protects both the integrity of the methods and the safety of those who would otherwise misuse them; readiness is a condition of transmission, not an obstacle to it.
conversion: An act of withholding that looks like hoarding for the gatekeeper's status actually functions as readiness-gating — restriction that appears to serve the teacher serves the work and its would-be practitioners instead.
